title: Tuesday Teacher Plan
note: No class Wednesday (minimum day). Thursday is build day for every grade, Friday is the one turn-in.

4th Period.topic: Factory Method: plan a new brick
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can plan one new brick type: the attribute that picks it, and 2 ways its instance is different from a normal brick.
4th Period.exitTicket: Plan your new brick type: what attribute picks it, and how is its instance different from a normal brick?
prep: Worked example (makeBrick with the strong brick) on the projector
Factory method video ready to replay the animal part (about 1:46–2:50)
Exit ticket posted on Google Classroom

segments.title: Wayground quiz
segments.do: Launch the Tuesday review Wayground: closed box, factory method, attributes, instance, selection logic, makeBricks().
segments.why: Spiral review of Monday's vocabulary before using it to design.
tips: Start it before the bell.
Note the most-missed question for the review.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed questions, then read the SMART goal aloud.
segments.why: Fix misconceptions before students design with these words.
tips: If 'attribute' vs 'instance' was missed, use the arrow: attributes IN, instance OUT.
Have one student say the goal back in their own words.

segments.title: Mini-lesson: attributes pick the instance
segments.do: Put the animal factory next to the brick factory. Walk the 3 rows: attributes in, selection logic, instance out. Then the brick attribute table: color, hits, width/height, points.
segments.why: Bloom Understand: map the video's example directly onto their own game.
tips: Ask pairs: 'In the brick factory, what's the attribute? What's the instance?'
Keep the closed-box diagram up.

segments.title: We do: read the worked example
segments.do: Read makeBrick(x, y, type) together line by line. Students find each video word in the code: attributes, selection logic, instance, outside of the box.
segments.why: Fully worked round 1 (the strong brick). Their own brick is the real experiment.
tips: Read only. Nobody opens Copilot today.
Cold-call with think time: 'Point to the selection logic.'
Stress: their brick must be different from 'strong'.

segments.title: You do: plan your brick type
segments.do: Students pick a one-word type, 2 attributes that change with new values, and the row it goes in. Shoulder partners talk it through first, then check the list.
segments.why: Bloom Apply/Create: designing the mechanic is what's assessed, not the code.
tips: Orally rehearse before writing (ELD and IEP support).
No ideas? 'Think of a game you like: what makes some blocks harder or worth more?'
If their bricks never disappear, steer them to color + size instead of hits.

segments.title: Exit ticket: the brick plan
segments.do: Students write their plan as the exit ticket on Google Classroom using a sentence frame.
segments.why: The exit ticket IS the plan, so Thursday's build starts from it.
tips: Read both frames aloud.
Check a few: type name + 2 values + a row.
Allow dictation or speech-to-text.

watchFor: Students copying the strong brick. Their type must be new.
Students opening Copilot to build. Today is plan-only.
Vague attributes ('cooler'). Ask for the actual value: color: "gold".

6th Period.topic: TinkerCAD Truss Bridge: build the deck
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my 5 triangles sit on top of a flat bridge deck, lined up in a straight row using the Align tool.
6th Period.exitTicket: What does a bridge deck do, and what do the triangles above it do?
prep: TinkerCAD open on the projector with Monday's 5 triangles
TinkerCAD class code on hand for sign-in problems
Exit ticket posted on Google Classroom

segments.title: Wayground quiz
segments.do: Launch the Tuesday review Wayground: rigid, truss, chords, diagonals, Duplicate and Repeat.
segments.why: Spiral review of Monday's concept and tool.
tips: Greet at the door.
Note the most-missed question.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Review the most-missed questions, then read the goal aloud.
segments.why: Front-load the goal before tech is on screens.
tips: Have a student repeat the goal back.

segments.title: What a deck is
segments.do: Show the deck diagram: the flat part people travel on; the triangles stand on it and keep it from bending.
segments.why: Concept first, so the clicks have a reason.
tips: Say 'deck' and have the class repeat it (ELL vocabulary).

segments.title: We do: build the deck
segments.do: Click along: Box → set 100 × 20 × 2 → select the 5 triangles → lift with the black cone, type 2 → drag them over the deck.
segments.why: Fully worked round, everyone at the same pace.
tips: Pause after each step for thumbs up.
Show where the white corner squares are and how to click the number to type.
If a student lost Monday's work: 1 Roof + Ctrl + D 4 times.

segments.title: We do: line them up with Align
segments.do: Select everything → L → middle dot on the long side → middle dot on the short side → spin the view to check.
segments.why: Align is the key precision tool for Thursday's top chord.
tips: If the deck moves instead, Ctrl + Z and click again.
Have students check from the front AND side views.

segments.title: You do: check and fix
segments.do: Students check their bridge against the 3 boxes and fix anything floating, sinking, or off the deck.
segments.why: Self-check builds independence; you circulate to the students who need you most.
tips: Check in first with anyone who had sign-in trouble Monday.
Early finishers: second side or a road (Future Engineer).

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom using a sentence frame.
segments.why: Checks the concept (deck vs. truss), not just the clicks.
tips: Read the question and frames aloud.
Allow dictation.

watchFor: Triangles sinking into the deck: lift them 2 with the black cone.
Align moving the wrong shape: Ctrl + Z, then click again.
Students who never got 5 triangles Monday: get them there first.

7th Period.topic: Warren Truss: draw the build plan
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group has a full-size drawing of one side truss measured with our paper measuring stick, and a cut list with the cut length and count for every piece of the whole bridge.
7th Period.exitTicket: How many diagonal pieces does your whole bridge need, and how did you figure it out?
prep: Paper: 2 sheets per student for measuring sticks + 2 per group for the drawing; tape and pencils
Groups of 4 decided (two Monday pairs together)
Group bags from Monday ready to hand back
Answer key is in the tips for the drawing, cut list, and exit ticket steps
Exit ticket posted on Google Classroom

segments.title: Wayground quiz
segments.do: Launch the Tuesday review Wayground: rigid, push test, brace, fair test, cutting along the flutes.
segments.why: Spiral review of Monday's evidence before they design with it.
tips: Hand back the group bags after the quiz, not before.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Review the most-missed questions, then read the goal aloud.
segments.why: Today has a lot of math. A clear target lowers anxiety.
tips: Hold up Monday's braced square: 'This is the whole idea of a truss.'

segments.title: I do: measuring stick, specs, cut length
segments.do: Fold a measuring stick live (sheet folded the long way 3 times; end to end for ½, then ¼ and ¾). Walk the specs: gap 1 stick, bottom chord 1½ sticks, equilateral triangles with ½-stick sides, 2 side trusses ¼ stick apart. Worked example: one diagonal = ½ stick + 1 glue square at each end.
segments.why: A shared unit replaces the ruler: same paper means every stick matches. Fully worked round 1 is one diagonal; the rest of the cut list is theirs.
tips: Ask: 'Why does everyone use the SAME paper?' (so measurements match)
Don't give the full cut list. That's the rigor this class asked for.
Ask: 'Why a glue square at EACH end?' (Monday's overlap).

segments.title: Groups of 4 and roles
segments.do: Join two Monday pairs. Students line up by birthday, youngest to oldest: Drafter (youngest), Measurer (second youngest), Materials Manager (second oldest), Checker (oldest). Group of 3: oldest is also Materials Manager. Group of 5: two Drafters.
segments.why: Complex Instruction: every role is needed; no one can finish alone.
tips: Say: 'No one is good at all of this. Everyone is good at some of it.'
Birthday order is random, so no one picks the 'easy' role, and status doesn't decide who leads.
The Checker has real authority: nothing is done until they say so.

segments.title: You do: draw one side truss
segments.do: Groups tape 2 sheets, trace the 1½-stick bottom chord with a dot every ½ stick, find each top point with two sticks folded in half, connect the top chord, label every piece in sticks.
segments.why: Bloom Apply: precise measuring and drawing to spec with a non-standard unit.
tips: Top point trick: two students each hold a ½-folded stick at a bottom dot and swing them together; where the ends meet is the top.
Publicly name careful folding and measuring when you see it (assign competence).
Answer key, one side: bottom chord 1½, top chord 1, 6 diagonals of ½.

segments.title: You do: make the cut list
segments.do: Materials Manager lists every piece for the WHOLE bridge with drawn length in sticks and count, adds a glue square at each end, then totals the sticks. Checker runs the checklist.
segments.why: Bloom Analyze: double for 2 sides, add cross pieces, work with fractions of a stick.
tips: Answer key, whole bridge: bottom chords 2 × 1½, top chords 2 × 1, diagonals 12 × ½, cross pieces 4 × ¼ (one at each bottom joint).
Total drawn length: 3 + 2 + 6 + 1 = 12 sticks, plus 20 pieces × 2 = 40 glue squares.
1½ sticks (about 42 cm) may be longer than their cardboard: they can join two strips with a glue square.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom using a sentence frame.
segments.why: Checks the doubling idea (one side vs. the whole bridge).
tips: Correct answer: 12 (6 per side × 2 sides).
Read the question and frames aloud; allow dictation.

segments.title: Clean up + bag the plan
segments.do: Pencils back. Plan AND measuring sticks go in the group bag with Monday's shapes and first names.
segments.why: Thursday's build starts from this plan, so it can't get lost.
tips: Thursday they measure and cut with these same sticks, so they can't get lost.

watchFor: Sloppy folds. Edges must line up before creasing, or every piece is off.
Cut list for one side only. It must cover both sides plus cross pieces.
One student doing everything. Point back to the roles.

accommodations: Agenda on the board, goal reviewed after the quiz, chunked numbered steps, worked example before you do, checklist, sentence frames, frequent check-ins. Get attention before directions; give them spoken, written, and shown.
Video words (attribute, instance, selection logic) and bridge words (deck, chord, diagonal) tied to a picture. Partner talk before writing. Two sentence frames per exit ticket.
Lexend Deca handouts, large type. Read steps and code aloud. Text-to-speech and speech-to-text OK. Spelling not graded.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer. 6th has movement and hands-on roles. Seat near the demo. If/then for non-preferred steps. Discreet redirection, fidgets, break pass.

Extended time and dictation on the exit ticket. Shortened floor: 8th plans 1 changed attribute; 7th gets the deck under the triangles (Align optional); 6th draws one triangle and its cut length. Supportive group placement. Fraction strip (the folded stick itself) OK for adding.
Future Engineer (OPTIONAL), pick one for 1 KB point.
frameworks: Every grade plans or builds toward Friday's product: a new brick type in their game, a TinkerCAD Warren truss, a cardboard Warren truss that gets load-tested.
6th: 4 roles with real authority (Checker). 7th and 8th: shoulder partners. Publicly naming competence.
Same routine as Monday, one exit ticket only, nothing else turned in, worked example first so success is guaranteed.
8th Understand/Apply (design a mechanic). 7th Apply (precision tools). 6th Apply/Analyze (measure with a shared unit, scale up to the whole bridge, add fractions).
